title: Slow Down!
transcript: Welcome back to Followers Review, where I review your games every single day until I hit 100,000 followers. Today is day eight, and I am going to review one of the games of Arfa. If you want me to review your game, all you have to do is like this video, follow me, and leave a comment with your chess.com username under this video, and only under this video. Please stop sending me messages. And this is actually quite an interesting one because Arfa, I've had a look at a few of your games, and I think before we talk about any strategy and like positional mistakes and tactical mistakes and stuff like that, we need to talk about your blunders because in pretty much every single game I found, you play one-move blunders. You give up a full piece for nothing. It happened here from a winning position to a checkmate in one move, and it happened here on just the third move of the game. And one thing that stood out to me is that whenever you played these moves, you've used here 3 seconds, here you used only 2 seconds, and okay, here you used 18 seconds. So, that's a little bit more of a full-on blunder. But what I'm trying to say is slow down. In your bio, you say chess and chill, but here I am seeing the chess, but I am not seeing the chill. So, before any move, ask yourself, is the square I'm going to defended by something? And this is defended by something, and so was the other pawn you took. And in a position like this one, you need to be aware of the checks. The only check that white has available in this position is this one. And so, it has to be registered in our brain that the queen can take the F7 pawn. And when you're moving something like a pawn, you need to ask yourself what lines you're opening up, not only for yourself, but for your opponent. And that's how we see the fact that the bishop is now able to see the F pawn, and we can avoid a tragedy. So, my advice to you is slow down, do some more puzzles, and in any position, check for your opponent's checks, captures, and threats. Good luck.
